newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to scrap foreign venture tax breaks July 1.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to scrap foreign venture tax breaks July 1.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament voted on Wednesday to scrap breaks on taxes and customs duties to foreign investment joint ventures from July 1.

Changes include repealing tax-free status on profits earned by joint ventures that were started prior to January 1, 1995, and halting exemptions on payment of duties for joint ventures importing goods to start their businesses.
Parliament also gave the government a month to submit a law on granting breaks to joint ventures engaged in industrial production, which the Ukrainian government has hoped to boost.
Finance Minister Ihor Mityukov told parliament the tax and customs breaks cost Ukraine 1.19 billion hryvnias last year.
Ukraine has attracted only $1.4 billion in foreign investment since independence in 1991 and investors complain about inconsistent laws, high taxes and corruption as the largest deterrents.
Mityikov said there has been almost zero growth in the number of joint-venture businesses created in the recent past.
